name: 2026-11-04-unprefixed-experimental-package-names
title: Name new experimental packages without the experimental prefix

attrs.decision:
New experimental packages use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>` and never the `experimental` prefix. Each one is declared in `EXPERIMENTAL_PACKAGE_NAME_EXCEPTIONS` in the [experimental package policy](../../../../scripts/experimental-package-policy.ts), because isolation checks and plugin-record ownership recognize an unprefixed experimental name only through that map. Promotion moves the package and removes its map entry; its npm name stays the same.

Existing packages with the prefix are listed in `LEGACY_PREFIXED_EXPERIMENTAL_PACKAGE_DIRECTORIES`. `pnpm run constraints` rejects the prefix in any other directory and rejects a listed directory that no longer holds a prefixed package, so the list can only shrink. A legacy package is renamed when it is promoted; renaming it earlier needs the release and migration evidence that the [plugin identity decision](2026-10-06-web-desktop-plugin-identity-compatibility.md) requires.

name: 2026-11-12-cua-program-tool-without-presets
title: CUA program tool for Agents without a preset

attrs.decision:
When `agentPreset` is a preset ID, only Agents on that preset receive raw `cua`. Every other Agent receives `cua_run_code`, including Agents without a composed preset and every Agent of a composition without the preset registry. The registry is an optional dependency of the provider: the provider recomputes the tool form of each live Agent when the registry loads or unloads, and without the registry no Agent counts as being on the configured preset. `agentPreset: false` still registers raw `cua` globally and creates no program runtime.

This partially supersedes [CUA programs outside the PTC preset](2026-11-09-cua-program-tool.md), which gave Agents without a composed preset neither tool. That note still owns the program tool's runtime, its initialization, and the choice of one tool form per Agent. It also changes one consequence recorded in [What stays host-plane once presets own the agent plane](2026-08-10-host-plane-ownership-after-presets.md), where an Agent that joined no preset received no tool. That note still owns the rule that entry points join Agents explicitly and that no check rejects an Agent for joining no preset.

Existing deadlines, cancellation, heap limits and control-message limits still apply. Finalization prioritizes the required completion value or bounded failure diagnostic within the combined payload budget. Truncated diagnostics preserve their failure kind. Required completion values remain lossless and fail if they cannot fit.

This supersedes only captured-output termination and diagnostic reclassification in [typed tool returns](../feature/2026-07-20-ptc-typed-tool-returns.md), and overflow-driven state disposal in [retained PTC](2026-09-23-best-effort-persistent-ptc.md). name: 2026-10-26-malformed-charset-declaration
title: Malformed charset recovery prefers UTF-8

attrs.decision:
`decoderForCharset` preserves valid single-label declarations and the absent-header UTF-8 default. If a declaration is unsupported as a whole, it checks its comma- and whitespace-separated labels for UTF-8, including standard aliases. A match selects a fatal UTF-8 decoder; otherwise the declaration fails before the response body is read and the provider cancels the stream.

The provider decodes once. Recovery rejects invalid UTF-8 with `WEB_UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE` and preserves the decoding error as its cause. Only an actual byte-cap truncation enables streaming decode, which omits an incomplete suffix and keeps `truncated: true`. Complete responses, including those exactly at the cap, validate the final sequence at EOF.

UTF-8 recovery is an explicit heuristic, not proof of the original encoding. The bytes `C2 A9` represent `©` in UTF-8 and `漏` in GBK; repeating them preserves that ambiguity at any length. The provider accepts that ambiguity for UTF-8 recovery but does not extend it to arbitrary legacy-encoding guesses.

name: 2026-11-13-draft-attachments-across-session-switches
title: Draft attachments across Session switches

attrs.decision:
**A draft with attachments holds its Session's scope.** While a composer draft has attachments and its Session is not removed, the input hub holds the Session with a `draft` reference that keeps no event connection, as [Session retain facets and recently viewed Sessions](../architecture/2026-11-15-session-retain-facets-and-recent-views.md) defines. Switching away and evicting the Session from the recent views therefore keep the same composer shell and its attachments: an active upload keeps running, a failed upload keeps its in-place retry, and a pasted image keeps its bytes in memory. Removing the last attachment, sending it, or removing the Session releases the hold; scope teardown then releases every attachment the draft still holds.

**A reload reports discarded attachments instead of restoring them.** On `pagehide`, the input hub marks each Session whose draft holds attachments in browser storage; a back-forward cache restore clears the marks. A composer mounted with a mark shows the "add them again" notice.
attrs.problem: Switching to another Session and back emptied the composer's attachment rail while its text survived (issue #5070). The Session scope disposer released every attachment the retiring composer held and revoked image previews, and nothing could rebuild them.

English | [中文](2026-07-06-recallable-compaction.zh.md)

## Problem

Compaction is irreversible from the model's current context. The summary the model sees carries no reference to what it shadows — `shadowedRange` lives only on the log-only `compaction/summary` event — and no tool lets the model read a shadowed span back. Whatever the summarizer drops is unavailable to the model, even though the append-only log holds every byte.
